question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-2, 0\right],$ compute $P\left(V \leq -\dfrac 12\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $V$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(v) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq v \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-2, 0\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(v) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2}, \quad &-2 \leq v \leq 0,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} P\left(V \leq -\dfrac 12\right) &=P\left(-2 \leq V \leq -\dfrac 12\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{-2}^{-1/2} f(v) \, \textrm dv \\[5pt] &= \int_{-2}^{-1/2} \dfrac{1}{2} \, \textrm dv \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-\dfrac 12-\left(-2\right)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 34. \end{align*} \]

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-4, 0\right],$ compute $P\left(X \lt -\sqrt{2}\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-4, 0\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{4}, \quad &-4 \leq x \leq 0,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(X \lt -\sqrt{2}\right) &=P\left(-4 \leq X \lt -\sqrt{2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{-4}^{-\sqrt{2}} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{-4}^{-\sqrt{2}} \dfrac{1}{4} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-\sqrt{2}-\left(-4\right)}{4}\\[5pt] &= 1 - \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{4}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0, 5],$ compute $P( X \leq 3).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[0,5],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{5}, \quad &0 \leq x \leq 5,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P(X \leq 3) &= P(0 \leq X \leq 3) \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{1}{5} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3-0}{5} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{5}. \end{align*}

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-5,-2],$ so it has the following probability density function:

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[k, 11k\right],$ where $k$ is a positive number, compute $P\left(0 \lt X \lt 6k \right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[k, 11k\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{10k}, \qquad &k \leq x \leq 11k,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(0 \lt X \lt 6k \right) &= P\left(k \lt X \lt 6k \right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{k}^{6k} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{k}^{6k} \dfrac{1}{10k} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{6k-k}{10k}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[0, 12\right],$ compute $P\left(-1 \leq X \leq 3 \right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[0, 12\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{12}, \qquad &0 \leq x \leq 12,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(-1 \leq X \leq 3 \right) &= P\left(0 \leq X \leq 3 \right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3} \dfrac{1}{12} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3-0}{12}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-7, 3\right],$ compute $P\left(-5 \lt X \leq 1\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-7, 3\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{10}, \qquad &-7 \leq x \leq 3,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(-5 \lt X \leq 1 \right) &= \int_{-5}^{1} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{-5}^{1} \dfrac{1}{10} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1-(-5)}{10}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{5}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-\dfrac 12, 2\right],$ compute $P\left(-1\leq V < \dfrac 12\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $V$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(v) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq v \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $V$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-\dfrac 12, 2\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\begin{align*} f(v) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{2}{5}, & -\dfrac 12 \leq v \leq 2, \\[6pt] 0, & \text{otherwise.} \end{cases} \end{align*}

So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} P\left(-1\leq V < \dfrac 12\right) &= P\left(-\dfrac 12\leq V < \dfrac 12\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{-1/2}^{1/2} f(v) \, \textrm dv \\[5pt] &= \int_{-1/2}^{1/2} \dfrac{2}{5} \, \textrm dv \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\dfrac 12-\left(-\dfrac 12\right)}{\dfrac 52}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{5}. \end{align*} \]

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-h, 5h\right],$ where $h$ is a positive number, compute $P\left(0< X \leq 3h\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \qquad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-h, 5h\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{6h}, \qquad &-h \leq x \leq 5h,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} P\left(0< X \leq 3h\right) &=\int_{0}^{3h} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3h} \dfrac{1}{6h} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3h-0}{6h}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*} \]

exampleAnswers.title: Computing a "Greater Than" Probability for a Uniformly Distributed Continuous Random Variable

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right],$ compute $P\left(X \gt 1\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[\dfrac{1}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{2}, \qquad &\dfrac{1}{3} \leq x \leq \dfrac{7}{3},\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(X \gt 1\right) &=P\left(1\lt X \leq \dfrac{7}{3}\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{7/3} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{7/3} \dfrac{1}{2} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{7}{3}-1\right)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{3}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $U$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-\dfrac 52, \dfrac 32\right],$ compute $P\left(U \geq 0\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $U$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(u) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq u \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $U$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[-\dfrac 52, \dfrac 32\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(u) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{4}, \qquad &-\dfrac 52 \leq u \leq \dfrac 32,\\[6pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} P\left(U \geq 0\right) &=P\left(0\leq U \leq \dfrac 32\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3/2} f(u) \, \textrm du \\[5pt] &= \int_{0}^{3/2} \dfrac{1}{4} \, \textrm du \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac 32-0\right)}{4}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{3}{8}. \end{align*} \]

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{9}{2}\right],$ compute $P\left(X \geq 1\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $X$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq x \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $X$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{9}{2}\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{4}, \qquad &\dfrac{1}{2} \leq x \leq \dfrac{9}{2},\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(X \geq 1\right) &=P\left(1\leq X \leq \dfrac{9}{2}\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{9/2} f(x) \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \int_{1}^{9/2} \dfrac{1}{4} \, \textrm dx \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{9}{2}-1\right)}{4}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7}{8}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $W$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[3, 11\right],$ compute $P\left(W \geq 7\right).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $W$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(w) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq w \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $W$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $\left[3, 11\right],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(w) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{8}, \qquad &3 \leq w \leq 11,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\begin{align*} P\left(W \geq 7\right) &=P\left(7\leq W \leq 11\right) \\[5pt] &= \int_{7}^{11} f(w) \, \textrm dw \\[5pt] &= \int_{7}^{11} \dfrac{1}{8} \, \textrm dw \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{11 - 7}{8}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{2}. \end{align*}

question.text: Given that the continuous random variable $Y$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-3, 7],$ compute $P(Y > 3).$
question.explanation:
The probability density function for a uniformly distributed continuous random variable $Y$ on an interval $[a,b]$ is given by

\[ f(y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{b-a}, \quad &a \leq y \leq b,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

Our random variable $Y$ is uniformly distributed on the interval $[-3,7],$ so it has the following probability density function:

\[ f(y) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{10}, \quad &-3 \leq y \leq 7,\\[5pt] 0, \quad &\textrm{otherwise.} \end{cases} \]

So, we have

\[ \begin{align*} P(Y > 3) &= P(3 < Y < 7) \\[5pt] &= \int_3^7 f(y) \, \textrm dy \\[5pt] &= \int_3^7 \dfrac{1}{10} \, \textrm dy \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{7-3}{10} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2}{5}. \end{align*} \]
